## Introduction

This data story uses Tracking (In)Justice's (@TrackingInJustice) data set on police-involved deaths to analyze

## Research Question

How does the type of force used in police-involved deaths in Canada vary across police agencies between 2021-2025?

## Install Necessary Packages

```{r}
#install.packages("tidyverse")
#install.packages("janitor")
#install.packages("testthat")
#install.packages("skimr")
```

## Run Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(testthat)
library(skimr)
```

## Set the Seed

```{r}
set.seed(466)
```

## Read in the Raw Data File

```{r}
raw_data <- read_csv("Trackinginjustice-RawData.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Remove Names of Victims

```{r}
my_data <- raw_data |>
  clean_names() |>
  select(-full_name, -name_first, -name_last, -name_middle,
         -nickname, -details, -race)
```

## Look at the Data before Cleaning

```{r}
glimpse(my_data)
```

```{r}
head(my_data)
```

```{r}
tail(my_data)
```

```{r}
slice_sample(my_data, n = 6)
```

```{r}
my_data |> count(highest_level_force, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
my_data |> count(police_service, sort = TRUE) |> slice_head(n = 10)
```

# Cleaning

```{r}
my_data <- my_data |>
  mutate(
    date = dmy(date),
    year = year(date),
    age = suppressWarnings(as.integer(age)),
    highest_level_force = highest_level_force |> str_squish() |> str_to_lower(),
    police_service = police_service |> str_squish(),
    police_service = case_when(
      police_service == "South Simcoe Police" ~ "South Simcoe Police Service",
      police_service == "Saguenay Police Department" ~ "Saguenay Police Service",
      .default = police_service
    ),
    # One row has the province code "QB", which is not a valid code.
    # The police service on that row is in Quebec, so it is recoded to "QC".
    province = case_when(
      province == "QB" ~ "QC",
      .default = province
    )
  )
```

## Group Police Services into Agency Types

```{r}
my_data <- my_data |>
  mutate(
    agency_group = case_when(
      str_to_lower(police_service) == "unknown" ~ "Unknown",
      str_detect(police_service, ",|;") ~ "Multiple agencies",
      str_detect(police_service, "RCMP|Royal Canadian") ~ "RCMP",
      str_detect(police_service, "OPP|Ontario Provincial|Sûreté|Surete") ~ "Provincial police",
      str_detect(police_service, "Nunavik|Nishnawbe|First Nation|Tribal|Transit|Border") ~ "Other",
      .default = "Municipal/regional police"
    )
  )
```

## Check they are in the right groups

```{r}
my_data |>
  distinct(agency_group, police_service) |>
  arrange(agency_group, police_service) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

\`

```{r}
my_data |> count(agency_group, sort = TRUE)
```

# Run Tests

```{r}
expected_force <- c(
  "environmental force", "gunshot", "intermediate weapon",
  "other", "physical force", "restraint", "taser/cew", "unknown"
)

expected_groups <- c(
  "RCMP", "Provincial police", "Municipal/regional police",
  "Multiple agencies", "Other", "Unknown"
)

valid_provinces <- c(
  "BC", "AB", "SK", "MB", "ON", "QC", "NB", "NS", "PE", "NL", "YT", "NT", "NU"
)

test_that("dates parsed and fall in 2021-2025", {
  expect_s3_class(my_data$date, "Date")
  expect_false(anyNA(my_data$date))
  expect_true(all(my_data$year %in% 2021:2025))
})

test_that("highest_level_force only has expected categories", {
  expect_false(anyNA(my_data$highest_level_force))
  expect_true(all(my_data$highest_level_force %in% expected_force))
})

test_that("age is numeric and plausible", {
  expect_type(my_data$age, "integer")
  expect_true(all(my_data$age >= 0 & my_data$age <= 110, na.rm = TRUE))
})

test_that("every death has an expected agency group", {
  expect_false(anyNA(my_data$agency_group))
  expect_true(all(my_data$agency_group %in% expected_groups))
})

test_that("cleaning kept every row", {
  expect_equal(nrow(my_data), nrow(raw_data))
})

test_that("names of individuals were removed", {
  expect_false(any(c("full_name", "name_first", "name_last") %in% names(my_data)))
})

test_that("province codes are valid", {
  expect_true(all(my_data$province %in% valid_provinces))
})
```

```{r}
write_csv(my_data, "Trackinginjustice_CleanData.csv")
```

# Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
clean_data <- read_csv("Trackinginjustice_CleanData.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

glimpse(clean_data)
skim(clean_data)
```

```{r}
tibble(
  variable = c("age", "force type", "agency"),
  n_unknown = c(
    sum(is.na(clean_data$age)),
    sum(clean_data$highest_level_force == "unknown"),
    sum(clean_data$agency_group == "Unknown")
  )
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, colour = "white") +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "Number of deaths")
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  count(highest_level_force) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(highest_level_force, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Highest level force", y = "Number of deaths")
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  count(agency_group) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(agency_group, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Agency type", y = "Number of deaths")
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  tabyl(agency_group, highest_level_force) |>
  adorn_percentages("row") |>
  adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 1) |>
  adorn_ns()
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  add_count(agency_group) |>
  mutate(agency_label = str_c(agency_group, " (n = ", n, ")")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_infreq(agency_label), fill = highest_level_force)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "Agency type",
    y = "Proportion of deaths",
    fill = "Highest level force"
  )
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  tabyl(agency_group, highest_level_force) |>
  adorn_percentages("row") |>
  adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 1) |>
  adorn_ns()
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  add_count(agency_group) |>
  mutate(agency_label = str_c(agency_group, " (n = ", n, ")")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_infreq(agency_label), fill = highest_level_force)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Agency type", y = "Proportion of deaths", fill = "Highest level force")
```

```{r}
n_total <- nrow(clean_data)
share_gunshot <- round(mean(clean_data$highest_level_force == "gunshot") * 100, 1)
n_unknown_force <- sum(clean_data$highest_level_force == "unknown")
smallest_group <- clean_data |>
  count(agency_group) |>
  slice_min(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```
